headline: Apple preprint reports generalist-model control across simulated and real robot-manipulation tasks
summary: The Nov 6 Apple-affiliated preprint introduces AMP1, a reusable harness in which a generalist model observes a robot and directly writes and executes code to control its manipulator as a task unfolds. The authors report 85.6% success on RoboLab-120 with Gemini 4 Argon and 82.8% with Claude Opus 5.5, compared with listed specialist baselines of 49.2% and 42.9%. They also report 104 successes in 108 physical trials across 12 tasks and three Franka Research 3 robots using Opus 5.5 at high reasoning effort. These are paper-reported results, not independent reproductions. The paper reports that AMP1 is slow because much of each episode waits for model reasoning; model/API cost and physical-trial artifacts remain open.
